chunks: Oh, oh, how I yearn to see them! Go away now, O Kumayl, wherever you wish!

key_terms.رُؤْيَتِهِمْ: Their vision/sight (referring to the learned or virtuous)
key_terms.كُمَيْلُ: Kumayl ibn Ziyad, a companion of Imam Ali

ai.seo_question: What does Imam Ali mean when he says 'Oh, oh, how I yearn to see them' in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: This poignant exclamation by Imam Ali (AS) captures the spiritual yearning for the 'vision' of the righteous, a concept deeply rooted in Shia eschatology and the love for the Ahl al-Bayt. The immediate dismissal of Kumayl serves as a narrative pivot, marking the end of the introductory wisdom and the beginning of the profound 'Letter to Kumayl' on the stages of knowledge. This transition highlights the intimate, teacher-student dynamic characteristic of Nahj al-Balagha's pedagogical style.
